strings.prefs.title: Preferences
strings.prefs.oracle.options.allow_edit_tip: When enabled, source code loaded from the database (packages, procedures, triggers, …) can be edited in the editor. When disabled, database objects open as read-only.
strings.prefs.oracle.options.ask_save: Ask to save edited database source
strings.prefs.oracle.options.ask_save_tip: When enabled, closing or switching away from a modified database-sourced editor prompts you to save changes back to the database.
strings.prefs.oracle.options.allow_compile_reado: Allow compilation of read-only source files
When enabled, you can still compile (CREATE OR REPLACE) even if the source buffer is read-only. When disabled, compile is blocked for read-only sources.
strings.prefs.oracle.options.confirm_commit_roll: When enabled, Commit and Rollback ask for confirmation before changing the database transaction. When disabled, they run immediately.
strings.prefs.oracle.options.use_dba_views_tip: When enabled and the session has access, object browser and metadata queries prefer DBA_* dictionary views (broader visibility) instead of ALL_* / USER_*.
strings.prefs.oracle.options.unicode_enabled_tip: When enabled, the IDE prefers Unicode-aware character handling for client/session data exchanged with Oracle (recommended for most databases).
strings.prefs.oracle.options.check_charset: Check for client and server character set mismatch
strings.prefs.oracle.options.check_charset_tip: When enabled, connecting compares client and server character sets and warns if they differ, which can cause conversion or data loss issues.
strings.prefs.oracle.options.view_alias: Add column alias list for view DDL
strings.prefs.oracle.options.view_alias_tip: Controls whether generated CREATE VIEW statements include an explicit column alias list. Auto decides based on the view definition; Always / Never force the behavior.
strings.prefs.oracle.options.view_force: Use FORCE option for View DDL
strings.prefs.oracle.options.view_force_tip: Controls when CREATE VIEW … FORCE is emitted. Only for Exports applies FORCE in export scripts; Always / Never force or omit it everywhere.
strings.prefs.oracle.options.scheduler_timestamp: Use timestamp format for scheduler objects
When enabled, DDL and display for DBMS_SCHEDULER objects use TIMESTAMP-style date/time formats instead of DATE-only formats.
strings.prefs.oracle.options.owner_prefix_tip: When enabled, generated SQL and scripts always qualify object names with the owner/schema (e.g. SCOTT.EMP) even when the current schema would make the prefix optional.
strings.wizard.oracle.title: Oracle Client Wizard
strings.wizard.oracle.welcome.intro: The Oracle Client Wizard will take you through a few simple steps to select the Oracle Client, to select the network configuration, and to define the language formats and options.
strings.wizard.oracle.welcome.requires: PLSQL IDE requires an Oracle Client to communicate with your Oracle Servers.
strings.wizard.oracle.welcome.download: If you do not yet have an Oracle Client software installation, you can download the Oracle Instant Client package from the Oracle web site through the following link:
strings.wizard.oracle.welcome.after_install: After installation you can restart PLSQL IDE to finish the configuration.
strings.wizard.oracle.welcome.note: Note: you can always start the Oracle Client Wizard at a later time through Settings → Preferences → Oracle → Connection.
strings.wizard.oracle.oci.description: PLSQL IDE will use the Oracle Client Library to communicate with the Oracle Server.
strings.wizard.oracle.oci.empty: No Oracle Client libraries were found. Use Select Other… to locate the library file.
strings.wizard.oracle.tns.description: The network configuration directory (TNS_ADMIN) contains the sqlnet.ora and tnsnames.ora configuration files, which control how databases are accessed on the network.
strings.wizard.oracle.tns.empty: No TNS_ADMIN directories were found. Use Select Other… to choose a folder.
strings.wizard.oracle.nls.description: Define the settings for the language, character set, and data formats for your Oracle sessions in PLSQL IDE.

strings.status.oracle_disabled: Oracle feature is disabled. Rebuild with --features oracle
